findings.text: The parity test the node's done-when rests on never supplies waive_domain_check, so it guards only that the call can be placed, not that a stated waiver reason reaches the guard. CASES (line 71) gives the complete/land cases the kwargs {run_id, gate, dry_run} and no waiver, and `grep -rn waive_domain_check tests/` finds no test anywhere that passes one. The landing is therefore true of the code (remove the map entry and the empty-string default together and four tests redden, gate/negative-control.log) but not guarded at the seam that matters: re-point the map entry "waive_domain_check": "waive_live_run" in reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py:70 and both surfaces would still answer identically on every existing case, because the tool would forward an empty waive_live_run while the CLI forwarded an empty waive_domain_check — a value-carrying regression no assertion reddens on. Non-blocking because no assertion the run added is self-referential; the defect is an absent case, not a moving one.

_ACTION_OPTION_PARAM does not carry --waive-domain-check, the option the crew complete verb gained at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2144, so a duty whose printed command states that waiver renders through action_form as None (the whole command unrenderable) rather than as a crew(action="complete", waive_domain_check=...) call. The file's own comment at line 117 makes completeness load-bearing — "Every option the eight verbs accept is listed" — and this is the option the landed change is what makes the tool surface able to accept, so the tool now takes a parameter the renderer cannot emit. Non-blocking and outside the node's write scope (obligations.py is not among its declared paths), and no duty composes the option today, so nothing is broken at runtime; it is the next sibling node in this plan that will compose it.
